answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to lock a slashable bond and complete a unique, time-bound proof of work tied to its public key, like a spiral of sequential hashes that cannot be precomputed. Honest agents post the bond once and reuse it, while a fake-identity farm must fund a separate bond and burn fresh compute for every willow-thin alias it creates in its garden of accounts, making mass forgery linearly expensive.
